answer: Bonded vouching makes sybils expensive: each new agent must be co-signed by established peers who lock a stake as solid as basalt. If the newcomer misbehaves, that bond is slashed, so vouchers only back identities they trust. An attacker spinning up a spiral of fake agents has to fund a real bond per node and risk losing it all, turning cheap identity-forging into a costly jetty jutting into capital it cannot recover.
